transcript.content: Hello. Welcome to the clinic, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Ever since the divorce and moving into my own place, I keep forgetting basic things like paying bills and showing up for appointments, even when I write them down. It’s started causing some real problems, and I'm getting worried that something more than just stress is going on.
Along with these memory difficulties, have you also been feeling persistently down, sad, or lost interest in the things you normally enjoy?

No, I haven't really been feeling down or sad, and I still enjoy my usual hobbies. It's more that I'm just feeling completely overwhelmed and stressed by managing all of these new responsibilities on my own, and I'm really frustrated with myself for constantly forgetting things.
How long have you been experiencing this level of stress and worry, and is it mostly focused on your new living situation or does it spread to other areas of your life?

It's been going on steadily for about 11 months now, ever since I moved out after my divorce. It’s definitely not just at home, as it has spread to my work life too. I've been struggling to coordinate work orders, getting distracted during repairs, and my supervisor even gave me a warning recently.
Besides feeling stressed and overwhelmed, have you experienced physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, trembling, or trouble sleeping over these past 11 months?

No, I haven't really experienced those physical symptoms like muscle tension, trembling, or trouble sleeping. My struggles are mainly focused on the forgetfulness, spacing out, and organizational difficulties I mentioned.
Have you recently had any physical medical conditions, head injuries, or neurological illnesses diagnosed by a doctor around the time these memory problems began?
No, I haven't had any head injuries, physical illnesses, or neurological conditions diagnosed. As far as I know, I'm physically healthy.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention, forgetfulness, or organization when you were a child or during your school years?

Yes, looking back, I definitely had similar issues when I was a kid. My elementary school teachers used to write on my report cards that I was smart but kept spacing out, losing worksheets, and forgetting to turn in homework I’d actually finished.
Did these struggles with focus and organization continue through your teenage years and earlier adulthood, or did they mostly improve until the recent divorce?

I'm not entirely sure and don't really recall how things were during my teens and twenties, but I seemed to manage okay back then. At least, I didn't notice them being this bad until the recent divorce and move.
Before your divorce, did you rely on your spouse or specific routines to help you stay organized and keep track of daily tasks?

Yes, my spouse handled almost all of our household finances and scheduling, so I never had to manage those logistical things on my own. Now that I'm living alone, trying to handle a new house, bills, and a more demanding lead maintenance role at work has made these organizational struggles very obvious.
Before your divorce, did you ever experience difficulties with concentration, finishing tasks, or restlessness in your previous jobs or personal hobbies?

I did sometimes get distracted and leave minor repair jobs half-finished or have to reread work instructions, but it didn't cause major issues because my workload was much simpler back then. I've never
Along with these focus issues, have you ever struggled with physical restlessness, difficulty sitting still, or acting impulsively without thinking, either now or when you were younger?

No, I've never really struggled with physical restlessness, difficulty sitting still, or acting impulsively. For me, the issues have always been more about spacing out, losing track of things, and forgetfulness.
Do you find that you still struggle with focus, forgetfulness, or losing things even during your hobbies or when you are relaxed and not feeling stressed?

To be honest, I'm not really sure and haven't thought about it much. My mind has been so consumed by the stress of work and managing my new household lately that I haven't had much relaxed time or time for hobbies at all.

Before the divorce, even during times when your life was stable and relatively stress-free, did you still struggle with things like losing everyday items, spacing out, or needing extra effort to stay focused?

Yes, looking back, these struggles aren't entirely new and actually date back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, my report cards often noted that I was smart but would space out, lose worksheets, and forget to turn in homework I had already completed.
Before your divorce, did you often lose everyday items like your keys or phone, or find yourself spacing out during conversations with family and friends?

Yes, I definitely did lose my keys and drift off during conversations to some extent before the divorce, but it's gotten much worse and more noticeable over the last 11 months since I've had to manage everything on my own. Looking back, this has actually been a lifelong pattern for me, even going back to elementary school when I would constantly space out and lose my worksheets.

opening_question.question: Hello. Welcome to the clinic, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong history of inattention, organizational difficulties, and forgetfulness dating back to childhood (as evidenced by elementary school report cards). While his symptoms became significantly more impairing and noticeable following his divorce and transition to living alone due to increased executive demands, the history of childhood onset and persistent inattentive symptoms across multiple settings (work and home) supports a diagnosis of ADHD (ICD-10: F90.0). An adjustment disorder (F43.2) was considered due to the recent stressor, but the chronic, neurodevelopmental nature of the symptoms since childhood points to ADHD as the primary diagnosis.
